scenes.title: 두 표시가 움직이는 때
lines: First, follow the line counter. As new pieces are placed, look for a moment when the line count stays unchanged while the score moves.

scenes.title: 같아지는 줄 수부터 보기
lines: This time, compare the two line counts first. Find a moment when they match, then move your attention to the scores and the difference between them.

scenes.title: 알림의 이름 읽기
lines: Read the action label that appears with the moving pieces. The notice draws attention to what just happened, while the score shows a retained result.

scenes.title: 사라지는 알림과 남는 기록
lines: Separate the moment when the notice appears from the view after it passes. The total stays available for comparison after the notice is gone.

scenes.title: 같은 줄 수에서 비교하기
lines: At the observed moment when both line counts are twenty-seven, the left score is 14,096 and the right score is 17,016.

scenes.title: 다른 장면의 앞섬
lines: In the later shot, the left player has fewer cleared lines but a higher score. That lead is a state observed during play.

scenes.title: 이름을 따라 숫자 읽기
lines: Decide whether you are reading points or lines before following the values. A number without a name makes it hard to choose which result improved.

scenes.title: 다시 찾을 위치
lines: Pieces keep falling, while the places to find the total and line count remain stable. Look at those locations separately from the brief notices.

scenes.title: 실제 화면에서 다시 점검하기
lines: Read the score’s name, the comparison between players, and the moment when a value changes, in that order. These are different questions about the same play.

scenes.title: Choose what to value · separate paragraph candidate
lines: The clip does not expose the complete scoring table. In our own design, however, the action we value and its score label should agree.

scenes.title: Make the calculation readable · separate paragraph candidate
lines: A design can reveal important contributions before its total. As the animation expands, keep the number and its meaning unobscured.
